newsitem.title: USA: NBA BASKETBALL-PAYTON CONTAINS IVERSON AS SONICS CRUISE PAST SIXERS.
newsitem.headline: NBA BASKETBALL-PAYTON CONTAINS IVERSON AS SONICS CRUISE PAST SIXERS.

text.p: Gary Payton scored 26 points and thoroughly outplayed rookie sensation Allen Iverson as the hot-shooting Seattle SuperSonics breezed past the Philadelphia 76ers 118-94 on Monday.
Sam Perkins scored 22 points and Shawn Kemp added 21 and 15 rebounds for the Sonics, who shot better than 60 percent over the last three quarters.
Payton, the 1996 Defensive Player of the Year, had no problems containing the lightning-fast Iverson, the league's top scorer among rookies.
Iverson, who is averaging 23.9 points per game, was held to 12 points, his second-lowest total of the season.
"It was no special challenge," Payton said. "I'm going to play the same way against anybody. I don't come in here and think about matchups ... I think about getting the SuperSonics wins."
Iverson had 11 assists but seven turnovers. He shot 4-of-17 from the field, just 1-of-9 from three-point range.
Mark Davis paced the Sixers with 20 points and Jerry Stackhouse chipped in 19.
Philadelphia cut the deficit to 63-59 with 9:35 remaining in the third quarter on a three-pointer by Stackhouse, but Seattle scored eight of the next nine points.
A 10-0 Seattle run in the fourth quarter put the game away.
In Vancouver, Glen Rice scored 30 points and Dell Curry added 21 as the Charlotte Hornets ended their seven-game road trip on up note with a 107-91 victory over the Grizzlies.
Vlade Divac added 14 points and 10 rebounds and Anthony Mason just missed a triple double with 13 points, 12 rebounds and nine assists for the Hornets, who completed a 3-4 road swing.
Anthony Peeler scored 19 of his 23 points in the first half and George Lynch added 20 off the bench for the Grizzlies, who have lost seven of their last eight games.
